attributes.body_ja:
動詞（どうし）の連用形（れんようけい）につながるもう一（ひと）つの動詞（どうし）に、五段動詞（ごだんどうし）「切（き）る」があります。「切（き）る」は、「最後（さいご）まで (A) する」や「完全（かんぜん）に (A) する」という意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。主（おも）にエネルギーや材料（ざいりょう）など、それを行（おこな）うために必要（ひつよう）なものがなくなって、それ以上（いじょう）続（つづ）けられなくなるような状況（じょうきょう）で使（つか）われます。

また、「切（き）る」は「全力（ぜんりょく）で」や「精（せい）いっぱい」という意味（いみ）で使（つか）われることもあります。この場合（ばあい）、(A) という行動（こうどう）に１００（ひゃく）％（パーセント）の力（ちから）を注（そそ）いでいることを表（あらわ）します。
attributes.body:
Another verb that is often seen used after the conjunctive form of other verbs is the う - Verb 切（き）る 'to cut'. 切（き）る will give the (A) verb the nuance of being done 'to completion'. However, the 'completion' that is being conveyed with 切（き）る is usually caused by the running out of some kind of resource, like energy. Due to this, 切（き）る is often translated as 'to do (A) to the point of being unable to continue' (or not needing to continue), or 'to totally and utterly do (A)'.

Occasionally, 切（き）る may also be used to show that (A) is being done at 'full pelt', 'full steam', or 'full capacity'. In these cases, it is similar to 'to resolutely do (A)', and just means that 100% effort is being put into the action.

Both 切る and おわる attach to verb stems to express finishing an action, but with different nuances. おわる simply marks completion, e.g. 使いおわった ('I finished using it.'). In contrast, 切る often implies using something up, e.g. バターを使い切った ('I used up all the butter.') or doing something to the very end with full effort, e.g. ゴールまで走り切った ('I ran all the way to the finish line.').

first_relatable.title: 切る
first_relatable.meaning: To do something completely to the end, Utterly, Resolutely

attributes.body: 切る conveys the idea of doing something completely, which overlaps with one nuance of てしまう・ちゃう, but their usage differs. てしまう・ちゃう can imply that the action was unintentional or against one's will, which 切る cannot. In other words, 食べ切った simply means 'I ate all of it.', while 食べてしまった・食べちゃった also can have the meaning of mean 'I ended up eating it (even though I didn't intend to).', which 食べ切った cannot.

second_relatable.title: 切る

attributes.body: Both can attach to verbs to form compound words. 切る emphasizes full completion or decisiveness, e.g. '言い切る' ('say definitively') or '読み切る' ('finish reading'), focusing on doing something thoroughly to its end. 込む conveys depth or intensity of action, e.g. '考え込む' ('get lost in thought'), highlighting depth rather than finality.

attributes.body: These two expressions are opposite in meaning. 切る conveys resolution or the complete execution of an action, e.g. やり切る 'do it all the way' or 使い切る 'use up'. 切れない is its antonym, used to express not being able to see an action through to the end, e.g. 食べ切れない ('I can't finish eating it.').

For example, やり切る suggests 'do it thoroughly', while 考え抜く adds the nuance of overcoming difficulty in the thinking process.
